headline: The three-card CODE 05 diagnosis is derivable and the gold matches it; one security-alert document also tells agents to escalate when a customer reports a charge they did not make, which could lead a careful agent to transfer instead of filing the dispute.

issues.summary: Doc_..._039 lists 'Customer reports transactions they did not make' as a reason to escalate to the security team. The gold handles the Evergreen fraud in-channel (dispute, close, reorder) with no transfer.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039: "Escalate to security team when: ... Customer reports transactions they did not make"

doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_003 CODE 05 step 3: customer-initiated alert -> "Ask customer to verify recent transactions. If they confirm all transactions are legitimate, clear the alert."
gold[15] file_debit_card_transaction_dispute_6281, gold[17] close_debit_card_4721, gold[19] order_debit_card_5739; no transfer_to_human_agents
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that escalates first ends the episode before the dispute, close and order writes and fails. The dispute procedure (doc_031) plus the card-action mapping is the more specific guidance, so most agents will follow the gold.
issues.suggested_fix: Limit doc_039's escalation bullet to bank-initiated alerts, or add 'after filing a dispute and replacing the card' to it.

solution_check: Reconstructed per the CODE 05 order (status -> account -> fraud alert -> velocity): unfreeze Blue and clear its velocity block (reason velocity_clear; the two writes commute), and unfreeze GFF. On Evergreen, the customer-initiated alert is not cleared because the customer disputes the $499.99 TechZone charge: file card_present_fraud with pin_purchase (the customer cites the text), close fraud_suspected, and reorder PREMIUM tier EXPEDITED $0 + PREMIUM design $0 to the address on file. This matches gold[0..19].
prior_note: The prior review rated this task clean. The doc_039 escalation tension is minor and new.
notes: customer_max_liability_amount 50 is defensible because the customer reported the charge to the bank on 11/06 by replying to the fraud text. Counting from today's filing (11/06 -> 11/14, 5+ business days) would give the $500 tier (499.99 under a cap); this is the same liability-anchor ambiguity reported in 082/084-086, but here the script supplies a same-day report. The task file did not change in v1.0.1.
